sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
The week of 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-04 was a dispersion week under a flat index, not a broad risk-on melt-up and not a defensive rotation: SPY returned just +0.1% while single-name and sector spreads ran double digits, so the tape moved names, not the market. It was also not a bond-driven repricing — the 10-year sat at 4.77%, two basis points off its prior 4.79% — and not a fear event, with VIX at 14.32, down 0.88 points. The story was semis-and-hardware leadership against a software rout, plus an ag-input bid, all inside an index that barely budged.

## Memory and hardware led; software cracked

The widest sector spreads of the week were Memory/Storage and Cybersecurity, and they pulled in opposite directions. Memory/Storage rose 7.6% on the week, +7.5% versus SPY, with all four priced members (STX, WDC, MU, SNDK) carrying a usable bar. The single loudest name sits inside it: SNDK returned +17.2% for the window, +17.1% excess over SPY, the top-ranked single name of the week. Computer/GPU (+5.9%, +5.7% vs SPY, six of six priced) and Foundry (+5.4%, +5.3% vs SPY, four of four priced) rounded out the hardware complex, with DELL up 14.9% (+14.8% excess) as the standout there. The plausible mechanism is a demand-and-pricing bid concentrated in storage and boxes rather than a rates or macro impulse — the rotation table confirms the sector rank, with XLK the third-best sector at +0.9% (+0.7% excess) but nowhere near the storage move, which tells you the strength was sub-sector, not a broad tech beta. The counterevidence is that outperformance alone does not name a cause, and with no dated news feed available this week I cannot attribute it to a specific catalyst; treat the concentration as the observation, not the explanation. Confirming signal: Memory/Storage holds a positive excess vs SPY into next week's closes. Refuting signal: SNDK gives back its +17.1% excess and the basket median turns negative vs SPY.

Software went the other way. Cybersecurity fell 6.9% (-7.0% vs SPY, four of four priced) and Software/SaaS fell 4.7% (-4.8% vs SPY, six of six priced) — the two weakest sector rows on the board. The damage shows up in the single-name ranks: FIG fell 16.3% (-16.4% excess, the week's worst ranked name), CDNS -14.0% (-14.1% excess), SNPS -11.0% (-11.1% excess) and PANW -10.3% (-10.4% excess). CDNS and SNPS are the EDA pair inside Semi-Cap/EDA, which was the one semis sub-group that lagged at -1.5% (-1.6% vs SPY, eight of eight priced) — so the semis strength was decidedly not uniform: design tools and cyber sold off hard while memory, GPUs and foundry rallied. This is a genuine split within technology, not a sector-wide move, and it is the most important structural fact of the week. Confirming signal: Software/SaaS and Cybersecurity extend their negative excess vs SPY next week. Refuting signal: CDNS or SNPS recovers its double-digit excess loss as EDA stabilizes.

## An ag-input bid, with crude alongside

The el-nino-ag basket (DBA, MOS, NTR, DE, equal-weight) rose 6.6% on the week, +6.5% excess over SPY — the single largest sector-or-theme excess on the board and the top row of the rotation table on one-, four- and twelve-week horizons (+6.5, +13.3, +11.6 excess). The ranked single names carry it: DE +10.0% (+9.9% excess) and MOS +9.5% (+9.4% excess). The competing read is that this is an energy-and-commodity beta rather than a weather thesis — XLE was the second-best sector at +2.2% (+2.1% excess) and WTI crude printed 94.09 (+2.85%) on the latest commodity snapshot, so a general commodity bid is a live alternative explanation. What separates them is that ag inputs (fertilizer, equipment) outran energy by a wide margin, which is consistent with something specific to the ag complex rather than pure oil beta. The theme's kill conditions require dated NOAA ONI and CBOT inputs that I do not have this week, so I make no claim that any trigger is met or unmet. Confirming signal: DBA/MOS/NTR/DE hold positive excess vs SPY next week. Refuting signal: the basket's excess collapses toward XLE's, marking the move as energy beta not an ag-specific bid.

## Macro was quiet, and that is the point

The cross-asset backdrop did nothing to force the equity dispersion. The 10-year at 4.77% moved two basis points; high-yield spreads at 2.65% tightened one basis point; VIX at 14.32 fell 0.88 points; the broad dollar index at 118.7 is a post-window snapshot as of 2026-08-28 and carries no weekly claim. The gamma-flip level moved to 768.35 from a prior 770.19. None of these is a repricing large enough to explain 17-point single-name spreads, which is why I read the week as micro-driven. I will not infer complacency from the low VIX or tight credit — those are observations, not a positioning read. The policy path row shows a 9/16 hike probability of 55.7% as of 2026-09-04; that meeting is later context, not next week's business, and the frame flags it has no prior observation to compare against, so I treat it as a level, not a move.

The evidence limitation to state plainly: no dated news headlines were retrievable this week and no prior close-phase reports were on file, so every claim above rests on the priced sector, theme and single-name tables and the rotation ranks.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
The question for next week is whether the technology split persists or mean-reverts. The memory-and-hardware leadership (storage +7.5% excess, GPUs +5.7%, foundry +5.3%) and the software weakness (SaaS -4.8%, cyber -7.0%) are the two forces most likely to carry, because neither looks like index beta — SPY was flat — so both need their own footing to continue. The persistence case is that the rotation table already shows XLE and the ag theme leading on four- and twelve-week horizons too, suggesting the commodity-and-hardware tilt is not a one-week accident. The reversal case is that double-digit single-name moves (SNDK +17.1% excess, FIG -16.4% excess, CDNS -14.1%) are exactly the kind of spread that snaps back; watch whether the extreme winners hold their excess and the extreme losers stabilize rather than extend.

For the ag theme, the pivot is whether it decouples from energy. It led on all three rotation horizons, but XLE's +2.1% weekly excess and crude's +2.85% snapshot keep the energy-beta alternative alive. If the ag basket holds positive excess vs SPY while XLE fades, the weather-specific read strengthens; if the two move together, it was commodity beta. The theme's kill logic depends on NOAA ONI and CBOT inputs I cannot date this week, so I make no trigger claim — that is the first thing to verify when the inputs are available.

Macro is the reverse risk to all of it. Rates at 4.77%, spreads at 2.65% and VIX at 14.32 gave the dispersion room to run; a sharp move in any of them would compress single-name spreads regardless of the micro stories. The 9/16 hike-probability at 55.7% is later context, but it is the largest scheduled macro swing factor on the horizon and worth pre-positioning attention toward as it approaches — not next week's event, but the one after.

Net: the base case is continued dispersion under a quiet index, with hardware/memory leadership and software weakness as the two live legs and the ag bid as the highest-conviction theme by rotation rank. The observable that would flip the whole frame is a rates or vol shock that collapses the spreads — until then, the tape rewards names, not direction.
